response.text: {"beats":[{"sentences":[{"claimId":"faraday.claim.law","text":"A magnet moves towards a coil, and the flux through the coil changes while it moves."},{"claimId":"faraday.claim.law","text":"That changing flux gives an emf, and the emf equals the rate at which the flux changes."},{"claimId":"faraday.claim.law","text":"A faster change in flux gives a larger emf, so the needle of the meter swings further."},{"claimId":"faraday.claim.law","text":"When the magnet stops, the flux stops changing, and the needle falls back to rest."}],"beatId":"b2"},{"sentences":[{"claimId":"c.faraday.steps.roots","text":"The law multiplies the number of turns by the change in flux and divides by the time taken, which gives {expr:faraday.problem}."},{"claimId":"c.faraday.steps.roots","text":"Working it out, the emf is thirty volts."},{"claimId":"c.faraday.steps.check.1","text":"Now we check it by putting the emf back, which gives {expr:faraday.back}."},{"claimId":"c.faraday.steps.check.1","text":"Both sides match, so thirty volts is right for five turns, twelve webers and two seconds."}],"prompt":"What do we divide by?","beatId":"b3"},{"sentences":[{"claimId":"faraday.claim.avoid","text":"A tempting mistake is to divide the change in flux by the time taken and stop, which gives {expr:faraday.wrong}."},{"claimId":"faraday.claim.avoid","text":"But every turn of the coil adds its own emf, so leaving out the turns gives too small a value."}],"note":"Every turn adds to the emf","beatId":"b4"},{"sentences":[{"claimId":"faraday.q.recall.answer.b5","text":"The answer is {expr:faraday.q.answer}, which is eighteen volts."},{"claimId":"faraday.q.recall.answer.b5","text":"We multiply the turns by the change in flux and divide by the time, as in {expr:faraday.q.eq}."},{"claimId":"faraday.q.recall.answer.b5","text":"So the emf comes out the same way as in the worked example, with new numbers."}],"prompt":"What emf does the coil give?","beatId":"b5"}]}
